note: Dong et al., Front. Plant Sci. 2025 (peer-reviewed). The quote on VLM anomaly detection performing poorly is present. Zero-shot CLIP AUROC is 58.47% (Sec 4.6). FPR@TPR95 goes 43.88->7.05 at 16-shot and 15.38->0.71 at all-shot (Table 3, abstract). Caveats: all results are on PlantVillage only, with 12 healthy classes as known and 26 diseased as unknown. The 43.88/15.38 figures are the VLPT-MCM baseline, not zero-shot CLIP.

Novello, Dalmau, Andeol, arXiv:2403.11532, a preprint (no peer-reviewed venue listed). The abstract has all three quotes. It proposes conformal AUROC and conformal FPR@TPR95 as corrections with probabilistic conservativeness guarantees. 'Intertwined' is hedged with 'may be'.

Hacohen, Dekel, Weinshall, ICML 2022 (peer-reviewed). Both quotes are present: 'the uncertainty principle is only suited for the high-budget regime' (Intro) and 'perform on par with random selection or worse' (Sec 4.2.1). The abstract gives 93.2% on CIFAR-10 with 10 labels, +39.4% over random. The SSL framework is FlexMatch (Secs 4.1/4.2.3), but the abstract says only 'state-of-the-art semi-supervised methods'.

Prabhu et al., CLUE, ICCV 2021 (peer-reviewed). The text says uncertainty/diversity sampling are 'frequently underperforming even random sampling' (Sec 4.4). Numbers match. SVHN->MNIST at 30 labels: Random 77.7, Entropy 65.8, CLUE 83.9. DomainNet R->C at 1k labels: Random 51.5, Entropy 48.1, CLUE 52.9. The gains are modest except at very low budgets, e.g. +6.2 on SVHN->MNIST at 30 labels.

The numbers are correct (CLUE paper, ICCV 2021). SVHN->MNIST: Random 77.7/88.2/95.2 vs CLUE 83.9/89.4/94.5. DSLR->Amazon: Random 54.3/58.0/67.5 vs CLUE 56.4/60.5/70.5. The generalization is overstated. Gains shrink with budget only on SVHN->MNIST (+6.2, +1.2, -0.7). On DSLR->Amazon they grow (+2.1, +2.5, +3.0). 'Shrink as budget grows' holds for one of the two cited shifts, not in general.
